inputs.text: A university ceremony should not be used to demand silence from people who feel the institution has failed them. Calling protest a “spectacle” protects those in power by making visible dissent seem like the problem, instead of confronting the conditions that prompted it. Formal complaint channels are no substitute for real accountability when institutions can use them to delay change. Students and families deserve recognition, but respect also means hearing people who are calling for reform—not just protecting the appearance of order.
